definition: Inclination means a person's natural leaning toward something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word inclination. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know inclination should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Given any spare hour, Marguerite follows her inclination toward the water, sketchbook tucked under one arm.
A whim is far weaker than an inclination — it visits for an afternoon, while an inclination is the direction you tilt year after year.
Compulsion goes far beyond inclination — an inclination invites you gently, while a compulsion drags you whether you consent or not.

A leaning is a mild, early-stage preference — the first tilt, newer and fainter than an inclination. An inclination is that pull grown steady: a preference that holds for years, reliably enough that family can predict it. A month-old leaning may become a lifelong inclination.

A bent is a settled natural aptitude — a knack for a kind of work, as in a mechanical bent. An inclination is broader and softer: any direction you tend to drift, with no skill implied. An inclination toward music just means you're drawn to it; a bent means you're good at it.

An inclination is a leaning — the direction a person tilts when nothing pushes back.
It is gentler than a drive and quieter than a passion: you can note an inclination, indulge it, or overrule it, and the word keeps the image of a slope you naturally slide along.
Inclination is the gentle word for a leaning you notice in yourself or others — an inclination to hum, to tinker, to say yes.
Propensity (also in this unit) is stronger and more clinical: a built-in behavioral pattern, often one being tracked or managed.
You follow an inclination; you monitor a propensity.
